title: Fossil Picks Jaipur Maharaja Padmanabh Singh Over Bollywood Star for Signature Watches
excerpt: A royal polo player fronts Fossil's return to Swiss watchmaking, as analysts question what overexposed celebrity endorsements still deliver
body:
• Fossil has named Sawai Padmanabh Singh, the titular Maharaja of Jaipur and an India polo player, as global ambassador for its new Signature watch collection.
  • Exchange4Media argues the choice gives Fossil a story of its own, instead of another Bollywood star or cricketer seen endorsing many categories at once.
  • The Signature CS-1 line marks Fossil's return to Swiss watchmaking, with two models priced in India at Rs 57,995 and Rs 75,995.
  • The test, the analysis notes, is still the product: heritage may start the conversation, but design, quality and price will decide purchases.

Fossil could have done what watch and lifestyle brands in India usually do: sign a Bollywood star or a cricketer, put a familiar face on a billboard, and rely on recognition to do the work. Instead, for its new Signature collection, the American brand has named Sawai Padmanabh Singh — the titular Maharaja of Jaipur and a polo player who has represented India — as its global ambassador. The collection was unveiled at Jaipur's City Palace, with a campaign filmed against the city's architecture.

An analysis in Exchange4Media by Dr Annurag Batra sets out why the choice matters. Bollywood stars and cricketers are the endorsement default because they get a brand noticed. The problem is volume: the same celebrity may endorse many brands at once, so a consumer may remember the face and forget the brand. Leading stars also command substantial fees, on top of production and media costs.

A face that stands apart

Padmanabh Singh offers a different kind of recognition. He belongs to Jaipur's former royal family, moves in international social circles and has a sporting identity through polo, but he is not a familiar presence across advertising categories. That distinction, the analysis argues, can make people stop and take notice — a fresh face need not be an unknown face, only a distinct one that has not been used to sell everything else.

The Jaipur connection also gives the campaign a setting and a cultural identity that differ from standard studio advertising. In the campaign film, Singh is seen horseback riding, studying sundial blueprints and browsing his watch collection, with the timepieces woven into those moments under the theme “As Distinct As Your Signature.” Fossil is therefore selling a setting and a biography as much as a watch: heritage presented through a living person, rather than heritage printed on a dial.

What he is actually selling

The product underneath the ambassador is a step up for Fossil. The Signature line combines the brand's American design heritage with Swiss watchmaking, elevated materials and precision engineering, and marks Fossil's return to Swiss watchmaking, building on more than two decades of the company's presence in Switzerland. Its debut collection, CS-1 — for Case Study One — takes its name and design principles from the American Case Study Houses programme and its mid-century approach to purposeful design and material integrity.

The line has two models. The 38mm Three-Hand Date Automatic carries a Swiss automatic movement, and the 42mm Master Calendar Chronoquartz combines day, date, month and chronograph functions with a Swiss quartz movement. Both have domed sapphire crystals, record-inspired dial textures and the brand's Triple Diamond Quality insignia. In India they are priced at Rs 57,995 and Rs 75,995 respectively — firmly in the premium segment Fossil says it wants to expand in.

Fossil's executives framed the appointment in heritage terms. Melissa Lowenkron, the brand's chief brand officer, said Singh was a natural choice because he “honors heritage while expressing it in a way that feels personal and contemporary.” Johnson Verghese, managing director of Fossil India, said Signature is a milestone in expanding the brand's premium watch presence, aimed at consumers seeking enduring quality and meaningful design.

Why the gamble could work — and its limit

For diaspora and India-focused premium shoppers, the logic is legible. A watch is a style statement as much as a timekeeper, and a royal polo player from Jaipur signals taste, continuity and occasion in a way that a heavily exposed film star cannot. Singh's polo background matters here too: it gives him an identity beyond a title, which keeps the association from resting on ceremony alone.

The limit is the one the Exchange4Media analysis itself states. A royal title may get people talking, but consumers will still examine the watch — its design, quality and price — before buying. At Rs 57,995 and Rs 75,995, the Signature models will be compared with established Swiss and premium fashion-watch rivals, not with the ambassador's story. Fossil has bought itself a distinctive opening conversation in a crowded endorsement market. Whether it converts will be decided, as it always is, on the wrist.
